data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old High German word 'glisc' meaning 'glass' or 'bright' and 'clear'. This name may have originated from the Jewish name 'Glickel', which is a combination of the words 'glick' (happiness) and 'el' (God). In Christianity, it is also associated with Saint Giles, the patron saint of the sick, who was said to have been healed by a wild boar, and is therefore sometimes invoked for protection against wild animals or for healing.
